prompt:
Earnshaw plc has made an investment with a net present value (NPV) of £42,000 at 10% and a NPV of (£22,000) at 20%. Calculate the approximate Internal Rate of Return.

	31.0%
	16.6%
	15.0%
	13.4%
judge_reasoning: Candidate 1 correctly performs linear interpolation between NPVs at 10% (£42,000) and 20% (-£22,000) and arrives at 16.6%, matching the correct option. Candidate 2 applies incorrect algebra/trial approach and selects 31.0%, which does not follow from the interpolation. Candidate 3 is largely corrupted/inconsistent in its working, though it ultimately states 16.6%; due to the unreliable derivation, it scores lower than the fully correct solution. Candidate 4 computes an IRR of 13.4% and even includes an incoherent final boxed value, making it clearly incorrect.
